answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can use graph-theoretic trust ranking. Bounded random walks from verified seeds confine synthetic identities behind a topological cut, barring them from the honest peer garden. An adversary incurs the scarce cost of securing authentic peer attestations per identity, rendering revoked reputation proofs an inert relic. However, transmission latency over copper cabling distorts walk sampling, unfairly penalizing distant honest nodes.
